- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high unless sentiment supports sustained rally.
- If 3+ consecutive days of negative sentiment, model often fails to correct downward; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 0.5–1.0x recent average from forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overshoots mid-term trend; apply smoothing: average last 5–7 days’ true values before projecting next period.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment reversal.
